MCP.scenario.inspect: List the production directories, Topics and Collections I may read, with schemas and explicit relations. Find temperature measurements, query their latest values and the last hour of history, and identify records without samples. Do not infer relations from field names.
MCP.scenario.source: Read capabilities and current contracts first. Plan a reusable temperature normalization Stream (raw temperature multiplied by 0.1), shared by MQTT and HTTP Sources with separate instance parameters, record identity extraction and measurement Collection mappings. Preview with dryRun=true and list required scopes; wait for my confirmation before saving. Keep Sources disabled; do not write real credentials or start acquisition.
MCP.scenario.build: Check contracts and permissions. In one related batch, create Demo Factory/Workshop directories, station and measurement Collections, matching Topics and Records, and an App granted access only to these Collections. logic0intro: The AND function returns TRUE if all arguments are true; returns FALSE if any argument is false.
logic0example: AND({Chinese}>90, {Math}>90, {English}>90), returns true if all three scores are >90, otherwise returns false.
logic1intro: The OR function returns TRUE if any argument is true; returns FALSE if all arguments are false.
logic1example: OR({Chinese}>90, {Math}>90, {English}>90), returns true if any score is >90, otherwise returns false.
logic2intro: The TRUE function returns the logical value TRUE.
logic3intro: The FALSE function returns the logical value FALSE.
logic4intro: The IF function tests a condition and returns one value if true, another if false.
logic4example: IF({Chinese}>60, 'Pass', 'Fail'), returns 'Pass' when Chinese score>60, otherwise returns 'Fail'.
logic5intro: The IFS function checks multiple conditions and returns a value corresponding to the first TRUE condition.
logic5example: IFS({Chinese}>90, 'Excellent', {Chinese}>80, 'Good', {Chinese}>=60, 'Pass', {Chinese}<60, 'Fail'), returns evaluation based on score.
logic6intro: The NOT function returns the opposite of the given logical value.
logic6example: NOT({Chinese}>60), returns false if Chinese score is >60, otherwise returns true.
logic7intro: The XOR function returns the exclusive OR of all arguments.
logic7example: XOR({Chinese}>90, {Math}>90), returns false if both scores are >90 or both are <90; returns true if exactly one score is >90.
logic8intro: The ISEMPTY function checks if a value is empty text, empty object, or empty array.
math0intro: The ABS function returns the absolute value of a number.
math0example: ABS(-8) returns 8, which is the absolute value of -8.
math1intro: The AVERAGE function returns the arithmetic mean of the arguments.
math1example: AVERAGE({Chinese}, {Math}, {English}) returns the average score of three subjects.
math2intro: The COUNT function counts the number of items.
math2example: COUNT(John, Tom, Mike, Lisa) returns 4, which is the number of people.
math3intro: The FIXED function rounds a number to specified decimals and returns text.
math4intro: The INT function returns the integer part of a number.
math4example: INT(3.1415) returns 3, the integer part of 3.1415.
math5intro: The LOG function returns the logarithm of a number with the specified base.
math5example: LOG(100, 10) returns 2, which is the logarithm of 100 with base 10.
math6intro: The MOD function returns the remainder after division.
math6example: MOD(4, 3) returns 1, which is the remainder of 4/3.
math7intro: The MAX function returns the largest value in a set of values.
math7example: MAX({Chinese}, {Math}, {English}) returns the highest score among three subjects.
math8intro: The MIN function returns the smallest value in a set of values.
math8example: MIN({Chinese},{Math},{English}) returns the lowest score among three subjects.
math9intro: The POWER function returns a number raised to a power.
math10intro: The PRODUCT function multiplies all the numbers given as arguments.
math10example: PRODUCT({Price}, {Quantity}) returns total price, which is price multiplied by quantity.
math11intro: The SQRT function returns the positive square root of a number.
math11example: SQRT(9) returns 3, which is the square root of 9.
math12intro: The SUM function adds all the numbers specified as arguments.
math12example: SUM({Chinese}, {Math}, {English}) returns the total score of three subjects.
math13intro: The SUMPRODUCT function multiplies corresponding components and returns the sum of those products.
math14intro: The RANDOM function returns a random number between 0 and 1.
date0intro: The DATE function converts a timestamp to a date object.
date1intro: The DAY function returns the day of the month for a given date.
date2intro: The DAYS function returns the number of days between two dates.
date3intro: The DATEDIF function calculates the difference between two dates in years, months, days, hours, minutes, or seconds.
date3example: DATEDIF({OrderTime}, {PaymentTime}, 'h'), if order time is 9:00 and payment time is 10:30 same day, returns 1.5 hours.
date4intro: The DATEDELTA function adds or subtracts a specified number of days to a date.
date5intro: The HOUR function returns the hour of a timestamp.
date6intro: The MONTH function returns the month of a date.
date7intro: The MINUTE function returns the minute of a date.
date8intro: The NOW function returns the current date and time.
date9intro: The SECOND function returns the seconds of a timestamp.
date10intro: The TODAY function returns today's date.
date11intro: The YEAR function returns the year of a date.
text0intro: The CONCATENATE function joins several text strings into one text string.
text1intro: The EXACT function compares two text strings and returns TRUE if they are exactly the same, FALSE otherwise.
text1example: EXACT({Phone}, {WinningNumber}), returns true if they match, false otherwise.
text2intro: The LEFT function returns the specified number of characters from the start of a text string.
text2example: LEFT('Class 3B Ja.y Chou', 2) returns 'Cl', the first 2 characters
text3intro: The LEN function returns the number of characters in a text string.
text3example: LEN('Morning sun') returns 11, as there are 11 characters including space.
text4intro: The LOWER function converts text to lowercase.
text5intro: The RIGHT function returns the specified number of characters from the end of a text string.
text5example: RIGHT('Class 3B Jay Chou', 3) returns 'hou', the last 3 characters.
text6intro: The TRIM function removes leading and trailing spaces from text.
text6example: TRIM('   Lanzhuo Industrial Internet   ') returns 'Lanzhuo Industrial Internet'.
text7intro: The UPPER function converts text to uppercase.
text8intro: The TEXT function converts a number to text.
text9intro: The VALUE function converts text to number.

uns.importJsonPlacementSummary: Path levels organize the structure. Topics hold the data and must be placed directly under State, Action, or Metric.
uns.importJsonFullRulesMarkdown:
### Root Object
The root JSON object must contain a namespace array.

### Path Nodes
Use name + children to build the hierarchy.

Path nodes are containers only. They should not include fields.

### Topic Folders
State, Action, and Metric are special folders.

Topics must be placed directly under one of these folders.

The parent folder determines the topic type.

- State is for status, mode, alarm, condition, or current values.
- Action is for commands, triggers, or action requests.
- Metric is for numeric measurements, counters, KPIs, or time-series values.

### Topic Nodes
Topic nodes are leaf nodes under State, Action, or Metric.

A topic may include optional fields and topic settings.

### Topic Fields
fields is an optional payload field array for State and Action topics.

Metric topics must include at least one field with name and type.

Each field should include at least name and type.

Supported field types:
INTEGER, STRING, FLOAT, DOUBLE, BOOLEAN, LONG, DATETIME.

### Topic Options
enableHistory: Use string "TRUE" to enable historical persistence. Use "FALSE" or omit it to keep the default behavior.

mockData: Use string "TRUE" to create and bind a mock source flow. Use "FALSE" or omit it to skip mock data creation.

extendProperties: Optional custom key-value metadata for integrations or extension configuration.

### Import Format
Use name for each node and children for nested nodes.

Do not use CLI-style path or type fields in this page import format.
uns.importJsonAgentPrompt:
You are a Tier0 UNS JSON assistant.

Turn the user's manufacturing, MES, factory, line, station, equipment, quality, material, or traceability requirements into an importable UNS namespace JSON.

Output rules:
- Output only one valid JSON object.
- Do not output Markdown, comments, explanations, or extra text.
- Format JSON with 2-space indentation.
- The root object must contain a namespace array.
- Every node must use name; nested nodes must use children.
- Do not use CLI-style path or type fields.

UNS structure rules:
- Build a business hierarchy such as v1 / Plant / Area / Line / Station / State|Action|Metric / Topic.
- Topic leaf nodes must be placed directly under State, Action, or Metric.
- Do not place normal topic leaf nodes directly under business folders such as Plant, Area, Line, Station, Equipment, MES, Production, Quality, or Material.
- If the user provides a full path such as Plant/Line1/Metric/Temperature, split it into nested name and children nodes.

Modeling rules:
- Use Metric for measurements, KPIs, counters, numeric values, and time-series data.
- Use State for status, mode, alarm, current value, current job, recipe state, equipment state, or material state.
- Use Action for commands, triggers, operator actions, MES transactions, or control requests.

Topic options:
- A topic may include displayName, description, enableHistory, mockData, extendProperties, or fields when useful.
- Metric topics must include at least one field with name and type.
- Use string TRUE or FALSE for enableHistory and mockData.
- Field types must be one of INTEGER, STRING, FLOAT, DOUBLE, BOOLEAN, LONG, DATETIME.

Default behavior:
- Follow the user's requested structure and terminology.
- If the request is generic, generate a practical MES hierarchy covering Production, Line, Station, Quality, Material, Traceability, Equipment, and Maintenance where appropriate.
- Keep the JSON clean and not overly detailed unless the user asks for details.

fleet.ssh.unknownHelp: Connection interrupted or timed out. Remote termination is unconfirmed. Check the host before running the command again.
fleet.ssh.truncated: Output exceeded the storage limit and was truncated.
fleet.collaboration.networkHelp: Headscale status of the network identity associated with this Fleet node. Identity not linked does not imply that a separately configured Tailscale client is offline. Agent management and business connectivity are reported separately.
fleet.edit.conflictHint: The current center revision is r{revision}. Compare changes, load the center version, or retain your edits for manual merging against this revision. Nothing is overwritten or saved automatically.
fleet.edit.permissionHint: Allow authorized local Edge users to edit this resource’s center draft. This does not grant publishing, deployment or center administration. Revocation blocks subsequent reads and saves.
fleet.edit.allowEditing: Allow Edge editing for this resource
fleet.edit.failed: Operation failed. Check the connection and authorization; your current edits are retained.
fleet.edit.grantConflict: Authorization changed or could not be saved. Refresh and confirm again.
fleet.edit.offlineHint: The center is unavailable or access is denied. Only cached content is shown. Retained offline drafts do not change the running configuration.
fleet.edit.authorityHint: Managed by the connected center; executed on this Edge. Saving updates the authoritative center draft. Publishing and deployment remain center actions.
fleet.acquisition.edgeSourceHelp: One EdgeSource references one registered node. Direct bindings map published outputs into center Collections. Processing programs belong to center Streams.
fleet.acquisition.consumePauseHelp: Retain queued deliveries while processing is paused. Other consumers continue. Disabling consumption also stops accepting new events at an acknowledged boundary.
fleet.centerStream.help: Center Streams reference published outputs of existing Edge Sources. Each event triggers independently; context provides inputId, alias, source and fixed release. Saving does not execute. Publishing switches all inputs together after preparation; old deliveries retain their release. No implicit join.
fleet.centerStream.objectRequired: Mapping and parameters must be JSON objects
fleet.centerStream.pausePublished: Pause processing and retain backlog when published
fleet.centerStream.preparing: Preparing all inputs; previous release remains active
fleet.centerStream.stopPending: Consumption has switched. Waiting for Edge to confirm stopping removed inputs; in-flight events retain the previous release.
fleet.control.title: Control requests
fleet.control.deviceMismatch: The device field in the input JSON must match the selected device ID
fleet.control.confirmNotice: Confirmation queues execution on the Edge. Closing this page or the HTTP request does not cancel a device action.
fleet.control.discard: Discard unsaved Control settings? Submitted invocation records remain available.
fleet.control.intentNotice: New requests are saved for confirmation. Unknown outcomes are queried using the original invocation and are never automatically resent.
fleet.control.grantNotice: Only explicitly authorized Controls can be invoked by the center. Restrictions bind the capability version and parameters and are checked before execution.
fleet.control.noCenter: Connect to a center before authorizing device Controls.
fleet.control.schemaInvalid: Enter a valid JSON schema object
fleet.control.versionChanged: This Control has been redeployed. Review the new version and permitted device parameters before saving.
fleet.control.streamNotice: Choose device Controls separately from data inputs. The program declares context.requestControl(alias, input, businessKey). Saving does not execute; publication freezes targets. Requests require confirmation by default.
fleet.control.decision.historicalOrCausa: Suppressed: historical, resumed or causal event
fleet.control.decision.activeIntent: Suppressed: an active or unknown request exists
fleet.queue.full: Queue limit reached; waiting for consumption
fleet.queue.help: Shared across this node’s outputs and consumers. Includes pending payloads, fixed delivery configuration and row allowance; excludes database indexes and WAL. Limits do not discard unacknowledged data.
fleet.localPublication.title: Local output sharing
fleet.localPublication.help: Authorize the connected center to subscribe to selected outputs. This does not transfer Source management. Authorization alone does not upload data; a center consumer must activate it. Revocation preserves queued data and local collection.
fleet.localPublication.confirm: Change center access to this output?
fleet.localPublication.failed: Could not update local output authorization. Refresh to inspect the current revision.
fleet.adoption.selectionScope: Source connection settings and selected Bindings become center-managed. Other Bindings remain locally editable and continue running. The selected scope is fixed for this adoption.
fleet.adoption.fixedSelection: This Source retains a fixed adoption selection. Edit the selected Bindings or disable them; other Bindings remain on Edge.
fleet.credentials.localBoundary: Secrets stay on this Edge. Saving creates or rotates a reference; select it in the Source configuration and deploy separately.
fleet.credentials.failed: Unable to load or save Source dependencies. Refresh and check permissions and revision.
fleet.acquisition.removeEdgeSourceHelp: Disable direct bindings and referencing center Streams, then wait for their stop boundaries to be confirmed. Only the center Source reference is removed. Fleet nodes, Edge configuration, pending deliveries and business data are retained.
fleet.lifecycle.archiveSourceHelp: Disable this locally managed Source and all Bindings, stop its output consumers and sharing, and settle pending uploads first. Configuration, credentials and historical business data are retained. Center-managed Sources cannot be archived locally.
fleet.acquisition.authorizationRevoked: Center authorization revoked — republish the authorized consumer to resume
fleet.lifecycle.retireSourceHelp: Deploy disabled Bindings first, stop output consumers, and settle pending uploads. Retirement uses a fixed deployment and archives the Source on Edge after dependency checks. Configuration, credentials, checkpoints and business data remain. Existing snapshots cannot reactivate a retired Source. Locally owned Bindings cannot be retired by the center.
fleet.queue.storage.capacityReached: Storage limit reached; new input is paused
fleet.queue.storage.monitoringUnavailabl: Storage monitoring unavailable; new input is paused
fleet.queue.storage.invalidConfiguration: Invalid storage limits; new input is paused
fleet.queue.storageHelp: Measured physical usage. WAL and temporary files are shared by the database server. Limits stop new Fleet input; draining continues. Host disk monitoring is also required.
fleet.coverage.title: Possible input loss during subscription interruptions
fleet.coverage.help: A failed durable commit does not advance the cursor. Reconnection cannot guarantee upstream replay (MQTT uses clean sessions). Intervals are conservative; the number of lost events is unknown. The latest 20 intervals are retained with a summary of earlier intervals.
fleet.replay.analysisOnly: Recompute Collection data without device actions
fleet.replay.help: Choose a retained input version and a contiguous committed sequence range. This creates a separate job and can replace current Collection values with historical results. Control requests and device feedback updates are suppressed. Up to 1,000 events / 8 MiB per job, at most four active jobs; each job processes at most one event per second. Cancel stops remaining work and preserves completed effects.
fleet.workspace.bindingHelp: A binding belongs to this Source: it selects a fixed Stream release, acquisition parameters, mappings and Edge storage. Multiple Sources can reuse the same Stream program.
fleet.workspace.registrationNeeded: This node has not completed business registration. Network membership alone does not authorize acquisition; register it before testing or deploying.
fleet.ssh.waitReady: Connecting SSH. Input becomes available when the session is ready.
fleet.ssh.profileNeeded: An enabled SSH connection profile is required. Configure the target, account, credential reference and host fingerprint below, then save and test before opening a terminal.
fleet.resources.unavailable: Edge unavailable. Refresh and retry; unconfirmed changes are not marked successful.
fleet.resources.conflict: Version changed. Your changes have not been submitted. Review the latest configuration; older versions cannot overwrite newer ones.
fleet.resources.explanation: These are the execution node’s Source / Stream resources. Both ends can manage them. Drafts do not execute; publishing applies on the execution node. All writes check versions.
fleet.resources.stale: Edge is disconnected. Showing the last synchronized catalog. Reconnect to submit changes.
fleet.resources.reload: Load the latest version? This replaces your unsaved changes.
fleet.resources.publishConfirm: Publish this fixed version on the execution node?
fleet.resources.saved: Draft saved. Running configuration is unchanged
fleet.collections.selection: Select this Edge’s Collections to synchronize
fleet.collections.explanation: Synchronization is independent of Source configuration. The center creates node-isolated Collection mirrors under the selected directory. Records and samples use durable synchronization. Deselecting stops new synchronization and retains received data.
fleet.collections.saved: Selection saved; waiting for Edge to apply
fleet.stream.queueHint: Disabling local business storage keeps the transport queue. Outputs upload through the durable Edge queue and a center Stream writes them to a Collection.
fleet.stream.invalidOptions: Enter valid acquisition options, parameters, and mapping.
fleet.stream.edgeSourceHint: Reference an existing Edge and its published Stream outputs. Create a regular Stream with an output as input, then write to a center Collection.
fleet.resources.outdated: This draft is based on an older version. The current configuration is loaded. Review and save a new draft before publishing.
collectionStorage.title: Data storage
collectionStorage.hint: Choose where subsequent writes are stored. Changes save automatically. The center uses synchronized Collections with the same name. Existing data stays in place and queued data keeps its original target.
collectionStorage.noTargets: No authorized destination. Select a target from the center Fleet page.
collectionStorage.targetsFailed: Could not read center destinations. Check connection and permissions.
collectionStorage.loadFailed: Could not confirm current policy. Retry; the effective configuration was not changed.
collectionStorage.conflict: The policy changed or a Collection definition is not synchronized. Refresh and review before saving again.
collectionStorage.saveFailed: The policy was not changed. Check connection, definition synchronization, permissions and existing data mirrors, then refresh.
collectionStorage.deliveryHint: Enqueueing does not confirm center storage. Failed deliveries remain for retry; refresh to see current status.
collectionStorage.accepted: Write accepted, awaiting center storage. Check delivery status in Storage policy.
fleet.ui.agentUnavailable: Host Agent data is unavailable. Business connection and infrastructure availability are separate. Check that the Fleet Agent is running on the Edge and its Backend can reach the Agent, then refresh.
collectionStorage.atLeastOne: Select at least one storage location.
collectionStorage.notConnected: Connect to a center to enable center storage.
collectionStorage.defaultPending: Local storage remains effective. The first connection defaults to local and center after definitions and permissions are verified.
NamespaceGuide.title: Build your unified namespace
NamespaceGuide.hint: Create datasets and organize them in folders.
NamespaceGuide.records: Define fields for records and optional samples
NamespaceGuide.foldersHint: Group datasets by site, line, or equipment.
NamespaceGuide.connectHint: Connect sources and process data with streams.
SourceStream.httpHeadersHint: Default connection headers. Store authentication in credentials. Individual requests can override ordinary headers.
SourceStream.httpHeadersInvalid: Header names and values must be valid and unique. Authentication and transport control headers are not allowed.
fleet.ssh.statusFailed: Unable to read terminal status. Refresh and retry.
fleet.ssh.settingsFailed: The new configuration could not be verified or its revision changed. The previous configuration is retained. Check the account and port, then refresh and retry.
fleet.ssh.accountHelp: An Edge operating system account, not a Tier0 account. Prepare it on the Edge and authorize SSH certificate login before switching. Changes are saved only after a successful connection test. Container operations also require Docker access.
fleet.ssh.reason.SSH_WAITING_FOR_AGENT: Waiting for the Edge Agent to complete SSH preparation and public key exchange. Check that the Agent is updated and connected.
fleet.ssh.reason.SSH_INSTALLATION_REQUIR: The Edge terminal service is not prepared. Run the installer to update the Fleet Agent and SSH service.
fleet.ssh.reason.SSH_INSTALLATION_INVALI: The Edge SSH installation information is invalid. Check the installation result.
fleet.ssh.reason.SSH_NETWORK_UNAVAILABLE: The Edge overlay address is unavailable. Check the Tailscale connection.
fleet.ssh.reason.SSH_HOST_KEY_CHANGED: The SSH host identity changed and the connection was blocked. An administrator must verify the Edge identity before re-enrolling the node.
fleet.ssh.reason.SSH_CONNECTION_FAILED: Unable to verify the SSH connection. Check the Edge SSH service, network ACL, system account and port, then retry.
fleet.ssh.checkHelp: Check SSH using the currently saved address, account and port. This does not reissue the enrollment token or apply unsaved form changes.
fleet.ssh.portHelp: This changes the port used by the center, not the Edge SSH service or network ACL. The target must already listen on this port and allow access from the center.
fleet.ssh.candidateFailed: SSH could not verify the proposed account or port. The previous configuration remains active. Check the Edge listener, account permissions and network ACL.
fleet.ssh.versionConflict: The configuration changed while you were editing. Reset to current, review it and edit again. The newer version was not overwritten.
fleet.runtime.operationFailed: The Source/Stream operation reached the Edge but failed at runtime. Check the target service, protocol configuration and credentials on the Edge. localhost refers to the Edge.
fleet.edge.connectionHelp: Checks the center using the registered identity. Registration does not mean the center is currently available.
fleet.edge.network.title: Tailscale status
fleet.edge.network.help: Cloud connections require Tailscale. The first connection prepares the client automatically; a missing client does not mean the token is invalid. Node registration and connection verification follow network enrollment.
fleet.edge.diag.token: The collaboration token is invalid. Copy the complete token from the target center.
fleet.edge.diag.bootstrap: The center network endpoint could not be reached. Check connectivity, DNS, and HTTPS certificates. The system will retry automatically.
fleet.edge.diag.rejected: The center rejected network enrollment. Ask an administrator to check node authorization and the center network service logs.
fleet.edge.diag.agent: The local Fleet Agent cannot be reached. Check its service and local access configuration, then refresh.
fleet.edge.diag.client: The Tailscale client is unavailable. The first connection starts automatic installation. If this persists, check the installation task logs and Tailscale service, then refresh.
fleet.edge.diag.isolation: This installation lacks Tailscale state isolation support and cannot automatically join this center. Ask an administrator to check installation support for this platform. Resubmitting the token will not resolve this.
fleet.edge.diag.disabled: Networking is disabled at the center. Enable it there, then wait for automatic retry.
fleet.edge.diag.mode: The center type and network mode do not match. Check the target center configuration and obtain a new collaboration token.
fleet.edge.diag.identity: The local network identity does not match the target node. Ask an administrator to check the node binding and network state before creating or rebinding nodes.
fleet.edge.diag.expired: The Tailscale identity has expired or requires authentication. Restore authorization for this node at the center.
fleet.edge.diag.key: Network credentials could not be obtained or saved. Check node authorization at the center and permissions on the local Agent data directory.
fleet.edge.diag.login: Tailscale could not join the network. Check the center's network service address, connectivity, and node authorization.
fleet.edge.diag.profile: Tailscale network state could not be prepared or restored. Ask an administrator to check the Agent and network maintenance logs. The system will retry automatically.
fleet.edge.diag.initializing: Tailscale is starting. The system will retry automatically; you do not need to resubmit the token.
fleet.edge.diag.prepare: Connection preparation failed. Check the center service, Agent, and network maintenance logs. This does not necessarily mean the token is invalid.
fleet.edge.diag.businessTimeout: The center connection check timed out, so business connectivity is not yet confirmed. Refresh to retry. If this persists, check the center response and network latency; you do not need to re-enter the token.
fleet.edge.diag.businessFailed: The center connection check failed. Check the center service and two-way access, then refresh. Being online in Tailscale does not confirm business connectivity.
fleet.edge.diag.autoRetry: Connection is in progress. You do not need to resubmit the token.
fleet.edge.diag.endpoint: The center connection endpoint was not found (404). Ask an administrator to check the cloud gateway routes and center version, then reconnect.
fleet.edge.diag.submit: Configuration is incomplete. Check the token, center service, and local Agent status, then retry. Saved permissions and collection scope are retained.
fleet.edge.diag.status: Connection status could not be loaded. Configuration is temporarily unavailable. Check local services and select Refresh.
fleet.edge.diag.checking: Checking connection status. Configuration will be available when the check finishes.
fleet.edge.diag.localDisabled: Collaboration is disabled on this installation. Ask an administrator to enable it, then refresh.
fleet.edge.collectionHelp: Collection definitions synchronize automatically. Data writes follow the global storage policy; pending deliveries are persisted and retried.
fleet.edge.userHelp: Center-assigned users are applied automatically through the current synchronization channel. View synchronized accounts and committed results here.
fleet.access.help: Controlled by this Edge. Turning an option off blocks that remote capability while keeping local management available. The SSH option controls platform terminals, not other operating-system SSH access.
fleet.access.saveFailed: Permissions were not saved. Refresh and retry.
fleet.access.readOnly: This Edge allows read-only access to metadata.
fleet.access.sshDenied: SSH is not allowed by this Edge
fleet.ssh.resetHelp: Restore the account and port registered by the Edge installer, with automatic certificates. Apply only after a successful connection test; otherwise keep the current settings.
fleet.ssh.secretHelp: Leave blank to keep the saved credential. Changing account or authentication requires new credentials and a successful test. Saved secrets are never returned.
fleet.ssh.reason.EDGE_SSH_DISABLED: Remote SSH access is disabled by the Edge.
fleet.collections.scopeHelp: All Collections includes future Collections. Partial selection includes only the selected Collections; others use local storage and queries. Changes affect subsequent writes. Already queued events keep their original destination; historical data is not deleted or moved. Remote metadata management is controlled separately.
fleet.collections.policyNotSaved: Collection selection was saved, but the storage policy was not changed. Check the connection and definition synchronization, then retry.
fleet.detail.awaitingEdge: Waiting for Edge to connect. Use this node’s access token on the Edge to connect to this center. Host status and remote management will become available after connection.
fleet.detail.remoteUnavailable: Edge is not connected. Remote management is unavailable.
fleet.edge.tokenRetained: The token is saved securely. It is not displayed again. Leave it unchanged to keep the saved token.
fleet.edge.tokenSaved: Token saved. Connection and business registration are still being checked.
fleet.edge.previousCenterResults: The synchronization results below belong to the previously registered center: {center}. They do not indicate delivery to the requested new center.
fleet.edge.registrationMismatch: The requested center does not match the existing business registration. The token is saved, but the new center is not connected. Check the center’s collaboration and network configuration.
fleet.edge.switch.network: Connecting to the new center’s network
fleet.edge.switch.registration: Registering this Edge with the new center
fleet.edge.switch.verification: Synchronizing definitions and checking the new connection
fleet.edge.switchFailed: The switch is not complete. Check the new center and network services; it will retry automatically. Existing data and deliveries keep their original destinations.
fleet.ssh.reason.SSH_PORT_BLOCKED: The center Headscale policy does not allow this SSH port. Ask an administrator to allow center-to-Edge access to this port, then retry.
fleet.ssh.reason.SSH_POLICY_UNAVAILABLE: Unable to verify the center Headscale policy. Check the Headscale service and dedicated Fleet policy, then retry.
fleet.ssh.reason.SSH_TIMEOUT: The SSH connection timed out. Check Edge connectivity, its SSH service, firewall and userspace Tailscale forwarding. A timeout alone does not identify which one failed.
fleet.ssh.reason.SSH_PORT_REFUSED: The SSH port refused the connection. Check that SSH is listening on this port and that the firewall is not rejecting it.
fleet.ssh.reason.SSH_AUTH_REJECTED: The SSH service rejected login authentication. Check the OS account, credentials or certificate trust, and both clocks. Account permissions and the active configuration were not changed.
fleet.ssh.reason.SSH_HANDSHAKE_FAILED: The SSH handshake did not complete. Check that this port serves SSH and review the server protocol configuration.
fleet.ssh.reason.SSH_CREDENTIAL_INVALID: The center SSH credential is unavailable or invalid. For automatic connections check the center certificate store; for custom connections replace and verify the credential.
fleet.ssh.reason.SSH_PROXY_UNAVAILABLE: The center userspace Tailscale proxy is unavailable. Check its configuration and service status.
fleet.ssh.reason.SSH_ACCESS_UNAVAILABLE: Unable to read the Edge SSH authorization. Restore the center-to-Edge business connection, then retry.
fleet.ssh.reason.SSH_CA_PENDING: Waiting for the Edge to install this center SSH CA public key. Keep the Edge Agent online; the system retries automatically.
fleet.ssh.previousKept: The change was not applied; the previous configuration is retained.
fleet.edge.centerTypeMismatch: The Token center type is missing or does not match the center. Upgrade the center and reissue the Token.
SourceStream.readiness.ready: Platform preconditions are ready; the target resource still needs checking.
SourceStream.readiness.routeMissing: The operation route is not registered.
SourceStream.readiness.maintenance: The platform is under maintenance. Existing configuration remains readable.
SourceStream.readiness.runtime: The runtime is unavailable. You can still read configuration and disable resources.
SourceStream.readiness.worker: The async worker is unavailable. Synchronous operations are assessed separately.
SourceStream.readiness.expired: Runtime evidence has expired. Refreshing status.
SourceStream.readiness.credentials: The credential service is unavailable. Other configuration remains editable.
SourceStream.readiness.unsupported: Complete platform runtime evidence is unavailable. Check individual operations; execution still checks the target resource.
SourceStream.readiness.dependencies: Platform preconditions cannot be confirmed. Existing configuration remains readable; disable rechecks permissions and versions.
fleet.access.controlHelp: Disabled by default. Enabling permits new remote Control requests only when their published version, individual authorization and caller permissions also allow them. Existing authorizations become usable again; this does not authorize all Controls. Disabling does not cancel admitted actions or prevent reading their results.
fleet.edge.historicalDeliveryHelp: These events retain their original center and Collection targets. They are separate from the current connection status and are not deleted or redirected when switching centers.
nativeApp.trashConfirm: Move “{name}” to trash? A running App will stop. You can restore and start it again.
nativeApp.accessHint: All workspace members can open this App when the selection is empty. Select roles to require at least one match.
nativeApp.roleKeyHint: Use lowercase letters. Separate words with underscores.
nativeApp.roleLoadFailed: Could not load business roles. Try again.
nativeApp.invalidRoleFile: The package contains an invalid roles.json.
nativeApp.skipInvalidRoles: Skip this file and continue importing
nativeApp.rolePlanChanged: Workspace roles changed. Review the updated roles and confirm again.
nativeApp.title: App
nativeApp.cloudPending: Cloud App downloads are coming soon. Upload a ZIP package to install an App.
nativeApp.uploadHint: Click or drag an App ZIP package here
nativeApp.zipHint: Node.js source package with meta.json; up to 500 MB
nativeApp.zipRequired: Select a ZIP file no larger than 500 MB.
nativeApp.uploadFailed: Upload or validation failed. Please retry.
nativeApp.validating: Upload complete. Validating the ZIP package.
nativeApp.grantsHelp: No Collections are granted by default. Select Collections and record/sample permissions as needed, limited by your account permissions. UNS, Flow and Role resources are not imported.
nativeApp.collectionsFailed: Cannot load Collections. Check your permissions and retry.
nativeApp.metadataHint: Installation creates or reuses Collections, Sources and Streams together, with the data permissions shown. Matching namespaces, resource types and keys reuse the same resources. Conflicting definitions stop installation without overwriting existing configuration or data.
nativeApp.importResourcesInactive: New Sources are imported disabled and Streams as drafts. Configure credentials and validate in Connect before enabling and publishing. Existing resources keep their running state.
nativeApp.invalidGrants: Enter unique aliases and select a Collection and at least one permission for each grant.
nativeApp.samePackage: {name} ({version}) is already installed. This package is identical; no installation is needed.
nativeApp.updateExisting: Found {name} ({version}). Continue to update this App, keeping its URL and business data without creating a copy.
nativeApp.installFailed: Could not submit installation. Please retry.
nativeApp.installDone: Installation complete. The App is running.
nativeApp.pollFailed: Cannot read progress right now. Retrying automatically. Installation may still be running.
nativeApp.trustHint: Only install source packages you trust. Installation executes dependency, build and startup scripts. Apps run with your host user privileges.
nativeApp.ignored: These resources are retained as files but are not imported: {resources}
nativeApp.retainGrants: Updates retain current data grants. The previous version keeps running if the new version fails to start.
nativeApp.listFailed: Cannot load Apps. Please refresh to retry.
nativeApp.uninstallConfirm: Uninstall App “{name}” and revoke its credential? Collection data, uploads, logs and persistent files are retained.
nativeApp.actionFailed: App action failed. Check the logs.
nativeApp.logsFailed: Cannot read logs. Please refresh to retry.
nativeApp.localHint: Upload and install without a center connection
nativeApp.refreshCredsHint: Stop the app, refresh its credentials to apply current permissions, then start it again.
nativeApp.refreshCredsConfirm: Issue new credentials with current permissions for {name} and revoke its old credentials. Start the app when finished.
nativeApp.streamPolicy.title: Stream Request permissions
nativeApp.streamPolicy.hint: Set the Request actions this app may use. Each Request and its resources require a separate grant. After adding permissions, stop the app, refresh its credentials, then start it again.
nativeApp.streamPolicy.notReady: The app is not ready. Permissions can only be reduced.
nativeApp.streamPolicy.loadFailed: Unable to load permissions. Refresh to try again.
nativeApp.streamPolicy.conflict: Permissions changed elsewhere. Refresh before editing again.
nativeApp.streamPolicy.rejected: Unable to save. Refresh and check the app status and your permissions.
nativeApp.streamPolicy.unknown: The save result is not confirmed. Retry the original request before editing or closing.
NamespaceView.invalidValue: Enter a valid value for this field.
nativeApp.inheritedHint: These grants come from group membership. Update them in Groups.
nativeApp.workspaceRoleHint: Business roles apply across the workspace. Linked Apps: {apps}
nativeApp.assignmentMissing: The member, group or role is unavailable. Close this dialog and refresh.
nativeApp.roleInUse: The role is used by an App or has been deleted. Refresh and try again.
nativeApp.deleteRoleImpact: Deleting this role removes its assignments from these members and groups.
nativeApp.noAppRoles: This App declares no business roles. All active workspace members can access it.
nativeApp.directRolesHint: Direct assignments and group membership determine App access.
